title: Elementary etale devissage of a finite type module
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, where $s=f(x)$, $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, and $\mathcal F_s$ is its pullback to this fibre. Put $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, where support is the locus of nonzero stalks and dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-dimension]. There are etale pointed neighbourhoods $g:(X',x')\to(X,x)$ and $e:(S',s')\to(S,s)$ inducing isomorphisms of residue fields at the distinguished points, with $f g=e f'$ for a map $f':X'\to S'$, a closed immersion $i:Z'\to X'$ of finite presentation, a finite map $\pi:Z'\to Y'$ over $S'$, and a finite-type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal G$ on $Z'$. All four schemes $X',Z',Y',S'$ are affine, $i_*\mathcal G\cong g^*\mathcal F$, and $h:Y'\to S'$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ with geometrically integral fibres. Here geometrically integral means integral after every extension of the residue field of a fibre. There is a point $z'\in Z'$ with $i(z')=x'$, and if $y'=\pi(z')$ then $h(y')=s'$, $\pi^{-1}(y')=\{z'\}$, and $\kappa(y')/\kappa(s')$ is purely transcendental. Smooth and etale have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; finite and closed immersion have the meanings of [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion].
